column1: # xlings version-resolution conformance vectors
# Which version an install request selects from the versions a recipe
# declares. The unit test tests/unit/test_semver_vectors.cpp drives the
# resolver xlings installs with (pin_target_to_subos, then the catalog's
# version selection) with every vector below; another implementation of the
# same grammar can vendor this file and run it unchanged.
# FORMAT
#   One vector per line, four columns separated by a single TAB:
#     request    the version part of a request, as written after `@`
#                May contain spaces, never a tab.
#     available  the version keys the recipe declares for the platform,
#                comma-separated, no spaces. Every key names a concrete
#                version (no aliases, no `latest`).
#     active     the version active in the workspace, `-` for none.
#     expected   the version selected, or `none` when nothing is.
#   Lines starting with `#` and blank lines carry no vector.
# RULES THE VECTORS EXERCISE
#   1. A request that equals a declared key selects that key.
#   2. Otherwise the highest declared version satisfying the request wins.
#   3. A bare version of three or more segments is written-prefix equality,
#      floored at three segments: 1.7.0 matches 1.7.0 and 1.7.0.1, never
#   4. A bare version of one or two segments is the prefix range [v, next):
#   5. A prerelease is exact; a release request never selects a prerelease.
#   6. Operators: >=, >, <=, < (a space-separated list is a conjunction),
#      ^ (up to the next release of the first nonzero segment), ~ (up to the
#      next second segment), and the wildcards 1.2.* and 1.*. Ordering
#      compares segment by segment, numerically, a missing segment being 0.
#   7. A bare name selects the highest declared version.
#   8. An active version that satisfies the request, and that the recipe
#      declares, is selected; otherwise resolution proceeds as if nothing
#      were active.
# request
# rule 1: a declared key is selected as written
# rule 3: three or more segments are written-prefix equality
# rule 4: one or two segments are a prefix range
# rule 5: a prerelease is exact
# rule 6: operators
# rule 7: a bare name selects the highest declared version
# rule 8: an active version that satisfies the request is selected
